problem:
$\,$ $P$ is not a rhombus and $Q$ is not a rectangle.

What is the negation of the compound statement above?
worked_solution:
De Morgan's law posits that the negation of a conjunction of two statements is equivalent to the disjunction of the negated individual statements. It can be stated symbolically as follows.

$$
¬(A∧B)=¬A∨¬B
$$

So, the negation of our statement is

$$
\begin{aligned}\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,¬(P\text{ is not a rhombus}\text{ and }Q\text{ is not a rectangle}) & ≡¬((P\text{ is not a rhombus})∧(Q\text{ is not a rectangle})) \\  & ≡¬(P\text{ is not a rhombus})∨¬(Q\text{ is not a rectangle}) \\  & ≡(P\text{ is a rhombus})∨(Q\text{ is a rectangle}) \\  & ≡P\text{ is a rhombus}\text{ or }Q\text{ is a rectangle}.\end{aligned}
$$
